title: Warehouse stock with reservations
prompt:
A warehouse tracks items by name. Every item has an on-hand quantity and a reserved quantity; its available quantity is on-hand minus reserved. An item exists from the first time it is received; just before that first receipt it counts as on-hand 0 and reserved 0. Process the commands listed at the end in order. Each command prints exactly one line, sometimes followed by one extra line (see the last rule).
- `receive ITEM n`: add n to the on-hand quantity, creating the item if it is new. Print `ITEM on-hand H available A`.
- `reserve ITEM n`: if the item does not exist, print `ITEM unknown`. If n is greater than the available quantity, print `ITEM reserve rejected (available A)`. Otherwise add n to the reserved quantity and print `ITEM reserved R available A`.
- `release ITEM n`: if the item does not exist, print `ITEM unknown`. If n is greater than the reserved quantity, print `ITEM release rejected (reserved R)`. Otherwise subtract n from the reserved quantity and print `ITEM reserved R available A`.
- `ship ITEM n`: if the item does not exist, print `ITEM unknown`. If n is greater than the on-hand quantity, print `ITEM ship rejected (on-hand H)`. Otherwise subtract n from the on-hand quantity, subtract n from the reserved quantity but never let it go below 0, and print `ITEM shipped n on-hand H reserved R`.
- `count ITEM n` (a stock count found n units on hand): if the item does not exist, print `ITEM unknown`. If n is less than the reserved quantity, print `ITEM count rejected (reserved R)`. Otherwise set the on-hand quantity to n and print `ITEM adjusted by D`, where D is n minus the old on-hand quantity, written with a sign: `+4` for an increase, `-3` for a decrease, and `0` when nothing changed.
- Low stock: after a command that was neither rejected nor about an unknown item, if the item's available quantity is now below 5 but was 5 or more just before the command, print one more line `ITEM low stock`.
H, R and A always stand for the item's on-hand, reserved and available quantities after the command (for a rejected command, its unchanged quantities). After all commands, print a line `---` and then one line per item in alphabetical order: `ITEM: on-hand H, reserved R, available A`.
Commands, in order: receive bolt 12; reserve bolt 9; reserve nut 1; receive nut 4; reserve bolt 4; receive bolt 10; ship bolt 11; release bolt 1; reserve bolt 7; count bolt 6; count bolt 15; release bolt 7; ship nut 4; ship nut 1; receive washer 30; reserve washer 25; ship washer 1; count washer 26; count nut 0; ship bolt 15; receive bolt 5; release gear 2.
